To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the growth pattern of colon adenocarcimoma in granulation tissue is different from that in normal subcutaneous tissue.
the growth patterns of a rat colon adenocarcioma are different after transplantation into granulation tissue compared with transplantation into the undamaged subcutaneous connecti ve tissue.
the growth of a transplantable rat colon carcinoma in pre‐formed granulating tissue results in a morphologically invasive growth pattern.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the question of whether the stroma surrounding malignant tumors influences the growth pattern of the tumor.

the question of whether tumor cells in vivo are influenced in their growth pattern by the surrounding tissue and whether this phenomenon is of any importance for the development of the invasive tumor phenotype.
the question of whether a tumor can be „educated”︁ by its environment to become invasive.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the invasive morphotype is not a specific property of a malignant tumor, but is rather a consequence of the tumor‐stroma relationship.
the invasive morphotype is a result of a specific interaction between tumor and stroma, and not a result of the mere presence of tumor cells in a granulation tissue.
the invasive tumor growth pattern can be induced by the stroma.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
granulation tissue is a potent inducer of tumor invasiveness.
the stroma surrounding many human malignant tumors may stimulate tumor invasiveness.
tumor cells can be stimulated to invade the surrounding connective tissue by the induction of granulation tissue.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the tumor‐stromal interaction is a dynamic process that can lead to a more invasive tumor phenotype.
tumor growth is influenced by the microenvironment, and that the microenvironment can be modified by surgical intervention.
the stroma of the tumor environment can have a strong impact on tumor growth.
